summary: This is a two-channel programmable function generator built around an ESP32-S3 DevKit, with an ILI9341 touchscreen and a rotary encoder for the user interface. Each channel takes an AD9833 DDS waveform, attenuates it selectably, re-centres it and gains it up, sets its amplitude with an AD5452 multiplying DAC, adds a DC offset from an MCP4822 DAC, and drives a relay-switched 49.9 Ω output, all from ±12 V generated by an isolated DC-DC converter from a 12 V barrel-jack input.

blocks.name: power-input
blocks.purpose: The 12 V barrel jack feeds +12C through the on/off switch, and +12C supplies the ±12 V converter and the 5 V linear regulator.

blocks.name: analog-rails
blocks.purpose: The TMR 6-1222 generates the +12V and -12V rails that power every OPA2810, with bulk and local decoupling on both rails.

blocks.name: 3v3-logic-rail
blocks.purpose: The AP2112K-3.3 LDO makes +3.3V from +5V for the DDS chips, DACs, analog switch, display and encoder, and the ESP32 module's 3V3 pins are tied to it.

blocks.name: mcu-ui
blocks.purpose: The ESP32-S3 DevKit runs the instrument, drives the ILI9341 display and its touch controller, and reads the rotary encoder.

blocks.name: center-bias
blocks.purpose: U15A buffers a filtered 0.423 V reference (CENTER_BIAS) that both channels use to remove the DDS DC level, and U15B is tied off as an unused follower.

blocks.name: ch1-signal-chain
blocks.purpose: Channel 1 runs AD9833 → selectable attenuator → offset-removing gain stage → ×4 stage → multiplying-DAC amplitude control → I-to-V conversion → offset summing amplifier → CH1.

blocks.name: ch2-signal-chain
blocks.purpose: Channel 2 is an identical chain built on U7, U11, U13 and U12, producing CH2.

blocks.name: offset-dac
blocks.purpose: The MCP4822 dual 12-bit DAC sets the DC offset for each channel through RC filters.

blocks.name: ch1-output
blocks.purpose: A transistor-driven relay connects CH1 through a 49.9 Ω source resistor to the CH1 terminal block and pin socket.

blocks.name: ch2-output
blocks.purpose: A transistor-driven relay connects CH2 through a 49.9 Ω source resistor to the CH2 terminal block and pin socket.

parts.J3: This is the barrel-jack power input: pin 1 carries the incoming supply to SW2 and pin 2 is ground.
parts.SW2: This wire-connected on/off switch connects the barrel-jack supply to the +12C rail.
parts.C1: This 0.22 µF capacitor is the only capacitor on +12C and serves as the input capacitor for U2 and the 7805.
parts.U2: This TMR 6-1222 isolated DC-DC converter turns +12C into the +12V and -12V rails for the op-amps, with COMMON tied to GND and REMOTE left unconnected.
parts.U3: This LM7805 linear regulator makes +5V from +12C for the ESP32 DevKit, the relay coils, the 5 V offset references and the 3.3 V LDO.
parts.C2: This 100 nF capacitor decouples the +5V rail at the 7805 output and the LDO input.
parts.C32: This 1 µF capacitor is the bulk capacitor on +5V and the input capacitor for the AP2112.
parts.U16: This AP2112K-3.3 600 mA LDO makes +3.3V from +5V, and its EN pin is tied to VIN so it is always on.
parts.R31: This 0 Ω link ties the DevKit's 3V3 pins to the board +3.3V rail, which connects the module's own 3.3 V regulator output in parallel with U16.
parts.U1: This ESP32-S3 DevKitC-N16R8 controls the instrument: it drives the shared DDS/DAC SPI bus, the display/touch SPI, the encoder, the attenuator select lines and the output relays.
parts.DS1: This ILI9341 TFT module with touch controller shares SCK (GPIO4) and MOSI (GPIO5) between the display and touch, and its display MISO is not connected.
parts.SW1: This rotary encoder module, powered from 3.3 V, provides the CLK/DT quadrature signals and a push switch to the ESP32.
parts.U6: This AD9833 programmable waveform generator module is the channel-1 waveform source, selected by FSYNC on GPIO10.
parts.U7: This AD9833 programmable waveform generator module is the channel-2 waveform source, selected by FSYNC on GPIO39.
parts.SW3: This TS5A23157 dual SPDT switch lets GPIO21 (CH1) and GPIO47 (CH2) route each AD9833 output either directly (NC) or through a 39.2k/10k attenuator (NO) to func_in.
parts.R3: This 39.2 kΩ resistor is the upper leg of the CH1 attenuator (ratio about 0.203) used when SW3 selects NO1.
parts.R4: This 10 kΩ resistor is the lower leg of the CH1 attenuator and also the ground reference/load on func_in.
parts.R16: This 39.2 kΩ resistor is the upper leg of the CH2 attenuator (ratio about 0.203) used when SW3 selects NO2.
parts.R17: This 10 kΩ resistor is the lower leg of the CH2 attenuator and also the ground reference/load on func_in.
parts.U15: This OPA2810 provides CENTER_BIAS: section A is a unity-gain buffer of the 0.423 V divider, and section B is an unused follower with its input grounded.
parts.R25: This 68.1 kΩ resistor is the upper leg of the CENTER_BIAS divider from +3.3V, giving 0.423 V.
parts.R26: This 10 kΩ resistor is the lower leg of the CENTER_BIAS divider.
parts.C15: This 1 µF capacitor filters the CENTER_BIAS divider tap at the U15A input.
parts.U4: This OPA2810 is the CH1 gain stage: section A applies gain 1+2k/499≈5 relative to CENTER_BIAS to strip the DDS DC level, and section B adds a further ×4 gain to drive the AD5452 VREF.
parts.R5: This 499 Ω gain resistor connects U4A's inverting input to CENTER_BIAS, so that stage subtracts about 4×0.423 V.
parts.R6: This 2 kΩ resistor is the U4A feedback resistor that sets its gain to about 5.
parts.R9: This 1 kΩ resistor is the ground leg of U4B's feedback network, which sets the ×4 gain.
parts.R10: This 3 kΩ resistor is the U4B feedback resistor, giving the stage a gain of 1+3k/1k = 4.
parts.U11: This OPA2810 is the CH2 gain stage, identical to U4 (offset removal with gain about 5, then ×4).
parts.R18: This 499 Ω resistor connects U11A's inverting input to CENTER_BIAS and sets the offset-removing gain.
parts.R19: This 2 kΩ resistor is the U11A feedback resistor, giving a gain of about 5.
parts.R21: This 1 kΩ resistor is the ground leg of U11B's ×4 feedback network.
parts.R22: This 3 kΩ resistor is the U11B feedback resistor, giving a gain of 4.
parts.U8: This AD5452 12-bit multiplying DAC scales the CH1 gained waveform on VREF to set the output amplitude, with its current output going to U5A.
parts.U13: This AD5452 12-bit multiplying DAC scales the CH2 gained waveform on VREF to set the output amplitude, with its current output going to U12A.
parts.R7: This 10 kΩ pull-up holds the U8 SYNC line inactive while the ESP32 is in reset or booting.
parts.R23: This 10 kΩ pull-up holds the U13 SYNC line inactive while the ESP32 is in reset or booting.
parts.R24: This 10 kΩ pull-up holds the MCP4822 chip-select inactive while the ESP32 is in reset or booting.
parts.U5: This OPA2810 handles the CH1 output: section A is the I-to-V amplifier for the AD5452 (using the DAC's internal RFB), and section B sums the inverted DAC voltage, -5 V and 3× the DC-offset voltage to produce CH1.
parts.C21: This 1.5 pF capacitor across U5A's feedback (RFB to IOUT) compensates the multiplying-DAC output capacitance for stability.
parts.R29: This 4.02 kΩ resistor is the U5B input resistor from the amplitude-DAC output, giving that signal an inverting gain of -1.
parts.R12: This 4.02 kΩ resistor from +5V injects a fixed -5 V term into the U5B summing node so the MCP4822 offset can swing CH1 both negative and positive.
parts.R13: This 4.02 kΩ resistor is the U5B feedback resistor, giving the inverting inputs unity gain and the offset input a noninverting gain of 3.
parts.U12: This OPA2810 handles the CH2 output, identical to U5 (I-to-V for U13, then offset summing to CH2).
parts.C22: This 1.5 pF capacitor is the feedback compensation capacitor for the U12A/AD5452 I-to-V stage.
parts.R30: This 4.02 kΩ resistor is the U12B input resistor from the CH2 amplitude-DAC output.
parts.R14: This 4.02 kΩ resistor injects the -5 V offset term from +5V into the U12B summing node.
parts.R20: This 4.02 kΩ resistor is the U12B feedback resistor.
parts.U17: This MCP4822 dual 12-bit voltage DAC sets the CH1 (VA) and CH2 (VB) DC offsets, and its LDAC pin is grounded so writes take effect immediately.
parts.R11: This 1 kΩ resistor forms an RC low-pass filter with C20 between DAC_A and the CH1 offset input.
parts.C20: This 100 nF capacitor filters the CH1 DC-offset voltage at U5B IN+.
parts.R15: This 1 kΩ resistor forms an RC low-pass filter with C24 between DAC_B and the CH2 offset input.
parts.C24: This 100 nF capacitor filters the CH2 DC-offset voltage at U12B IN+.
parts.SW4: This SPDT relay (5 V coil) connects CH1 to the output resistor on its B contact, enabling or disconnecting the CH1 output.
parts.SW5: This SPDT relay (5 V coil) connects CH2 to the output resistor on its B contact, enabling or disconnecting the CH2 output.
parts.Q1: This 2N3904 is the low-side driver for the SW4 relay coil, controlled by GPIO41.
parts.Q2: This 2N3904 is the low-side driver for the SW5 relay coil, controlled by GPIO13.
parts.R8: This 1 kΩ resistor limits the Q1 base current from GPIO41.
parts.R27: This 47 kΩ pull-down holds Q1 off so the relay stays open while GPIO41 floats.
parts.R28: This 1 kΩ resistor limits the Q2 base current from GPIO13.
parts.R32: This 47 kΩ pull-down holds Q2 off so the relay stays open while GPIO13 floats.
parts.D1: This 1N4148 is the flyback diode across the SW4 relay coil (cathode to +5V).
parts.D2: This 1N4148 is the flyback diode across the SW5 relay coil (cathode to +5V).
parts.R1: This 49.9 Ω 2512 resistor sets the CH1 output source impedance at about 50 Ω and protects the op-amp from shorts.
parts.R2: This 49.9 Ω 2512 resistor sets the CH2 output source impedance at about 50 Ω and protects the op-amp from shorts.
parts.J1: This is the CH1 output terminal block (signal and ground).
parts.J4: This 2-pin socket carries the CH1 output in parallel with J1.
parts.J2: This is the CH2 output terminal block (signal and ground).
parts.J5: This 2-pin socket carries the CH2 output in parallel with J2.

nets.+12C: This is the switched raw 12 V from the barrel jack after SW2, and it feeds the ±12 V converter and the 7805.
nets.+12V: This is the positive analog rail from U2 that powers all OPA2810 V+ pins.
nets.-12V: This is the negative analog rail from U2 that powers all OPA2810 V- pins; C4, C6, C10, C12, C14 and C34–C36 decouple it even though it is typed as a signal net.
nets.+5V: This is the 7805 output that powers the ESP32 DevKit, the relay coils, the AP2112 and the 5 V offset-injection resistors.
nets.+3.3V: This is the AP2112 output that powers the AD9833s, AD5452s, MCP4822, TS5A23157, display, encoder and the CENTER_BIAS divider.
nets.Net-(R31-Pad1): This net carries the DevKit's 3V3 pins, which R31 links to the board +3.3V rail.
nets.Net-(U15A-IN+): This is the filtered 0.423 V divider tap that U15A buffers to make CENTER_BIAS.
nets.CENTER_BIAS: This is the buffered 0.423 V reference applied through R5 and R18 so the first gain stages cancel the AD9833 output's DC level.
nets.Net-(SW3A-COM1): This net carries the AD9833 (U6) output into the CH1 attenuator-select switch.
nets.Net-(SW3B-COM2): This net carries the AD9833 (U7) output into the CH2 attenuator-select switch.
nets.Net-(SW3A-NO1): This is the switched path through R3, which attenuates the CH1 waveform by about 0.203.
nets.Net-(SW3B-NO2): This is the switched path through R16, which attenuates the CH2 waveform by about 0.203.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH1/func_in: This is the CH1 waveform, direct or attenuated, entering the U4A gain stage.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH2/func_in: This is the CH2 waveform, direct or attenuated, entering the U11A gain stage.
nets.Net-(U4A-OUT): This is the bias-removed, ×5 CH1 waveform fed to the U4B ×4 stage.
nets.Net-(U11A-OUT): This is the bias-removed, ×5 CH2 waveform fed to the U11B ×4 stage.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH1/gained_func: This is the full-scale CH1 waveform driving the AD5452 VREF, which the DAC code then scales.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH2/gained_func: This is the full-scale CH2 waveform driving the AD5452 VREF, which the DAC code then scales.
nets.Net-(U5A-IN-): This is the AD5452 IOUT current-summing node, held at virtual ground by U5A.
nets.Net-(U5A-OUT): This is the amplitude-scaled CH1 voltage, which is fed back through the DAC's RFB and into the offset summer through R29.
nets.Net-(U12A-IN-): This is the CH2 AD5452 IOUT current-summing node.
nets.Net-(U12A-OUT): This is the amplitude-scaled CH2 voltage feeding RFB and the offset summer.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH1/5V_ref: This is the U5B inverting summing node, where the scaled waveform, the +5V injection and the feedback combine.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH2/5V_ref: This is the U12B inverting summing node, where the scaled waveform, the +5V injection and the feedback combine.
nets.DAC_A: This is the raw MCP4822 channel-A output that sets the CH1 DC offset.
nets.DAC_B: This is the raw MCP4822 channel-B output that sets the CH2 DC offset.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH1/dc_offset: This is the RC-filtered CH1 offset voltage at U5B IN+, which appears at the output with a gain of 3.
nets./Function_Generation/FG_CH2/dc_offset: This is the RC-filtered CH2 offset voltage at U12B IN+, which appears at the output with a gain of 3.
nets.CH1: This is the final CH1 op-amp output, routed to the SW4 relay common.
nets.CH2: This is the final CH2 op-amp output, routed to the SW5 relay common.
nets.Net-(SW4B-B): This is the relay-switched CH1 signal ahead of the 49.9 Ω output resistor.
nets.Net-(SW5B-B): This is the relay-switched CH2 signal ahead of the 49.9 Ω output resistor.
nets.Net-(J1-In): This is the CH1 output node at the J1 and J4 connectors.
nets.Net-(J2-In): This is the CH2 output node at the J2 and J5 connectors.
nets.Net-(D1-A): This is the low side of the SW4 coil, switched by Q1 and clamped by D1.
nets.Net-(D2-A): This is the low side of the SW5 coil, switched by Q2 and clamped by D2.
nets.Net-(Q1-B): This is the Q1 base drive from GPIO41, with a 47k pull-down.
nets.Net-(Q2-B): This is the Q2 base drive from GPIO13, with a 47k pull-down.
nets.GPIO11: This is the shared SPI data line to both AD9833s, both AD5452s and the MCP4822.
nets.GPIO12: This is the shared SPI clock line to both AD9833s, both AD5452s and the MCP4822.
nets.GPIO10: This is the FSYNC line for the CH1 AD9833 (U6).
nets.GPIO39: This is the FSYNC line for the CH2 AD9833 (U7).
nets.GPIO9: This is the SYNC line for the CH1 amplitude DAC (U8), pulled up by R7.
nets.GPIO40: This is the SYNC line for the CH2 amplitude DAC (U13), pulled up by R23.
nets.GPIO14: This is the chip-select line for the MCP4822 offset DAC, pulled up by R24.
nets.GPIO21: This line selects the CH1 attenuator path in SW3.
nets.GPIO47: This line selects the CH2 attenuator path in SW3.
nets.GPIO4: This is the SPI clock shared by the ILI9341 display and its touch controller.
nets.GPIO5: This is the SPI MOSI line shared by the ILI9341 display and its touch controller.
